transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. It's nice to meet you too. I'm mainly here because I just feel worn down almost all the time. Um, even after a full night's sleep, I still feel it. By the time I've handled work and tried to deal with the house clutter, I just have very little energy left for anything else.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yeah, I have. It's... most days there's just this low, gray mood kind of running in the background. I mean, I can still go into the lab and talk to people, so I'm getting things done. But I just don't really feel light or excited about things anymore. Even stuff I usually enjoy, um, like baking, or checking the telescope... I just don't feel it the way I used to.
How long have you been feeling this low mood?
It's been a while. I'd say this low baseline has been going on since... well, shortly after we moved into the older house. That was a little over two years ago.
Have you noticed a change in your appetite?
No, not really. My appetite has been pretty normal. I mean, I still eat about the same amount I usually do, so I haven't noticed any changes there.
During these past two years, have you felt down or depressed more days than not?
Yeah, I would say so. It's definitely more days than not. Like I mentioned, it's just kind of always running in the background most of the time.
During these past two years, was there ever a time when your low mood went away completely for as long as two months?
No, I don't think so. I really can't recall a time where it went away completely for that long. It's pretty much just been a constant thing... so, no, definitely not for two whole months.
Do you often feel hopeless?

Yeah, I do. I often catch myself assuming that the house will never really be settled. It just feels like I'm probably going to keep operating at this reduced level for good. It makes it really hard to look ahead or plan anything, like trips or... or future stargazing projects. I just kind of expect things to stay this way.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yes, I have. It's been pretty frustrating. Tasks that used to be pretty straightforward and sequential for me... like revising a paragraph for a grant proposal or even just picking out materials for a repair around the house... they just take me a lot longer now. It feels like my mind is moving slower, and I end up second-guessing all these little decisions that I used to just make without thinking twice about it.
Have you been feeling bad about yourself?

No, not really. I mean, I don't feel great about how little I'm getting done, but I wouldn't say I feel bad about myself as a person. I don't feel worthless or anything like that. I'm just... tired and stuck.
Have there been times during the past two years when your depression got bad enough that it significantly interfered with your ability to function?

Well, I wouldn't say I've completely stopped functioning or anything. I mean, I'm still getting my day-to-day lab work done. But it definitely interferes. Like I was saying, drafting grants and just making routine decisions for my projects take noticeably longer now. 

And at home... I've pretty much stopped keeping up with the things that used to structure my downtime. I haven't been doing any baking, or tending to my bonsai trees, or... or keeping up with my telescope plans. I'm still getting by, but I just don't have it in me to keep all those normal routines going right now.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

No, my sleep has actually been fine. I fall asleep without much of an issue and usually sleep right through the night. I know I mentioned feeling tired all the time, but it doesn't seem to be because I'm lacking actual sleep.
Do you often feel low on energy or fatigued?

Yes. That's honestly a big part of why I'm here. I just feel worn down almost all the time. Like I said, I'm getting a full night's sleep, but it doesn't seem to make a difference. By the time I've handled my work at the lab and tried to deal with the clutter around the house, I just have very little energy left for anything else.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energetic or unusually up for several days in a row?
No, I haven't. I've never really felt unusually energetic or anything like that. Just... just the opposite, mostly.
Did these feelings start after a specific stressful event?

Well, I wouldn't say it was a single stressful event, exactly. It's just... this low baseline, this feeling of being worn down, it's been going on since shortly after we moved into our current house. It's an older place, and that was a little over two years ago now.
During this two-year period, was there ever a time when for at least two weeks you had five or more depression symptoms at the same time?

No, I don't think so. It hasn't really been like a sudden, intense crash where everything hits at once for a couple of weeks. It's just been this... steady, low-grade feeling the whole time. Nothing really spikes, it just stays kind of flat and exhausting.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things?

No, not really. I mean, I worry about normal things, like bills or work, but I wouldn't say it's excessive. It's not like my mind is racing with anxiety or anything. I just feel... drained, you know? Not anxious.
Have other people noticed that you seem to move or speak more slowly than usual?

No, no one's ever said anything like that to me. I don't feel like I'm moving in slow motion or anything. I just feel tired, but I'm still getting around and talking the same way I always do, as far as I know.
Does this low mood cause you significant distress?

I'd say it's more frustrating than severe distress, but it definitely bothers me. I mean, I’m still getting my actual lab work done, but... things like writing grant drafts and making routine project decisions, they just take noticeably longer than they used to. 

And at home, it's just... I've kind of stopped keeping up with everything. I used to do a lot of baking, take care of my bonsai trees, get the telescope out... those things used to really structure my downtime. Now I just don't have the drive for them. So, yeah, it is upsetting to just be dragging through things like this.
Do you often have low self-esteem?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I know I'm capable, and I know I'm good at my job. I don't really feel bad about who I am or doubt myself... it's just the lack of energy that gets to me. So, no, my self-esteem is generally fine.
